rationale:
Decision: resubmit the iteration 10 design exactly as it was raced, with wheel_track 0.14. I reject the draft's changes and the critique's stated fix to the design.

Evidence. The outcome table is the authoritative record. Iteration 10 raced with wheel_track 0.14, mass 0.8, kp 4.0, kd 0.3, ki 0.2, base_speed 1.5, sensors at y=0.08 spanning x=-0.04 to +0.04 (0.02 m pitch, 16 mm footprints), weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], and line_loss last_direction. It scored 231.83, the best of all raced designs. Its dev-track results were oval 5/20 finishes (mean score 443.75, max_error 0.0585), s-bend progress 0.49 with 0/20 finishes, and slalom progress 0.12 with 0/20 finishes.

Discrepancy. The authorised entity1 text says iteration 10 used wheel_track 0.09, and the critique's loop-gain argument (narrowing track from 0.12 to 0.09 gives 1.33x yaw gain) is built on that value. The outcome table shows the raced value was 0.14, and iteration 6 at 0.12 with the same controller scored 138.64. So the raced best was a wider track with less yaw authority per PWM count, not a narrower one. Changing wheel_track to 0.09 would be an untested change that the evidence does not support. I therefore keep 0.14, which is the value that actually produced 231.83.

What I accepted from the critique: the draft's bundled changes (kp 5.5, mass 0.45/0.55, base_speed 1.0, ki 0.5, kd 0.8, wheel_track 0.08) are untested and cannot be attributed, and mass below the tested minimum is unjustified. Rejecting them is right for a final, unseen-track race. I also accept the critique's correction that other designs (iterations 4, 6, 8, 9) also have 20-trial multi-track records. Iteration 10 is the best-scoring measured design, not the only measured one.

What I did not claim: the off-track margin is thin (oval max_error 0.0585 against a 0.06 limit, s-bend 0.0631 above it), and the single persistent line-loss event per run is not fixed by any justified gain change. Base speed 1.5 produced the only finishes measured, so I keep it.

Expected result: roughly the iteration 10 record on development tracks (oval finish rate about 0.25, s-bend progress about 0.49). The unseen final track may be harder, and this design has no measured margin for a sharper bend. This is the least-risk option among the measured designs.
